title: Brown Long Grain Rice, Unenriched, Raw

content.title: About
content.content: Brown long grain rice is a whole‑grain rice that retains the bran and germ layers. It has a light brown color, a mildly nutty flavor, and a firmer texture than white rice. This unenriched, raw rice must be cooked before consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Because it is not milled, brown rice keeps more nutrients than white rice.
Long grain varieties stay separate and fluffy after cooking, making them popular in Asian dishes.
It provides more fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals than polished white rice.
Storing it in a cool, dry place extends shelf life, as whole grains are prone to oxidation.
In many regions brown rice is considered a more sustainable option because it requires less processing.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids normal muscle and nerve function and participates in energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6) are involved in carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds and ferulic acid help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white rice, brown rice raises blood glucose more slowly.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can bind minerals and reduce their absorption; soaking or sprouting lowers its level.

items.title: Long cooking time
items.content: Raw brown rice requires a longer cooking period than white rice, which may be inconvenient.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to rice.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rinse the rice under running water, then soak for about 30 minutes to improve texture. Cook using a 1:2 rice‑to‑water ratio: bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat for 40–45 minutes. Use the cooked rice in salads, pilafs, soups, or as a side dish with vegetables and proteins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, refrigerate or freeze to slow fat oxidation. Discard any grains that develop a rancid or moldy smell.
